Posted October 25, 2002
(MarijuanaNews note: The article below is further proof of Dr. Lester Grinspoon's thesis that the full medical potential of cannabis can only be realized with the full legalization of cannabis. It is also further evidence for my belief that we cannot give organized quackery control over the access to the plant.
See
Calling All Quacks: The Therapeutic Police State and the Politicization of Medicine. Doctors Cannot Study The Violence of Cannabis Prohibition. Because They Are The Disease, Not The Cure.

Many patients who need cannabis may have difficulty getting it, but none more so than the terminally ill who are confined to hospitals or hospices controlled by the medical establishment. These terminal patients, especially if they are elderly and unaware of their rights, are often under the total control of the specialists. Palliative care specialists are supposedly expert in reducing the pain and other suffering endured by the terminally ill or those with intractable conditions.

Most but not all of the medical uses of cannabis are palliative, which makes the debate about its medical utility all the more bizarre. FDA-style regulation was supposedly intended to protect patients against the hucksterism of the pharmaceutical industry, but it has been perverted into a system under which the industry can use state violence against the sick and dying to maintain the monopolies of the pharmaceutical companies and their agents in the medical professions.

FDA authority originally included only determining the safety of the pharmaceuticals, but it was later extended to include the efficacy of the drugs. The logic behind this added authority was to protect patients who might be deceived into using something ineffective and thus miss out on an effective treatment.

However, if a substance is used as a palliative, the results are highly subjective. If patients think that they are hurting less, who is the better judge of that, the patients or the specialists?

This is not to say that there is no need for the help of palliative care specialists. First, unlike cannabis, many of the drugs used to relieve pain have a very narrow range between an effective and a lethal dose.

Second, patients may have limited knowledge or impaired ability to make decisions because of their age or medical conditions.

Consequently, much more than a surgeon or radiologist, a palliative care specialist needs to have the humility to listen to the patients reports on what works for them. The existence of patient advocacy groups is strong evidence that the medical profession has been insensitive toward the suffering of patients, especially regarding the treatment of chronic or intractable pain.

In addition, there is other circumstantial evidence from the medical establishment that they know that pain is not being adequately treated. If there is no need for better pain treatment, why has the pharmaceutical industry spent so much money trying to develop new pain-relievers?

And if cannabis is not effective, why do patients want it?

The point here is that unless people are free to access cannabis without the approval of organized quackery, then we are all at risk of dying in agony at the hands of ignorant and arrogant agents of the therapeutic state. We should not wait until we are at the mercy of those who have arrogated to themselves the power to deny us our most basic rights when we are at our most helpless.

Live free, or die in pain!)

Palliative Care Doctors Cautious about Marijuana, Edmonton Conference Told

From The Canadian Press
October 22, 2002

Many doctors tending to the terminally ill are still extremely cautious about the use of medical marijuana despite growing pressure to embrace it.

Palliative care specialists attending a national conference in Edmonton were told Monday that clinical trials haven't yet shown that pot is an effective medical therapy for those with terminal illnesses. They also heard marijuana can produce negative side-effects, especially in older patients.

" Patients often get what we call disphoria, which is a sense of unwell-being, and this can last for hours, up to days, " said Dr. Ingrid de Kock of the Regional Palliative Care Program in Edmonton. " Patients might also go so far as to get hallucinations or acute anxiety attacks or acute mania.
(MarijuanaNews note: First, cannabis produces fewer dangerous side-effects than most legal drugs.
See
Meanwhile UK Painkillers Kill 2,000 Per Year. But They Are Sold Over-the-Counter So They Must Be Safe!

If older patients are afraid to use cannabis, and consequently have disphoria when they do, it could be the result of a life-time of reefer madness, reinforced by the ignorance and prejudice of the quacks.)

 " We have so many medications that have better side-effect profiles in palliative care patients, that do an even better job than what marijuana possibly can. "
(MarijuanaNews note: In any other context, the claim that there is adequate treatment for pain would be met with outrage and derision.)

De Kock said there's growing pressure by some patient advocacy groups for doctors to embrace medical marijuana.

Some patient groups have complained they're not getting enough help from the medical community in applying for legal exemptions that allow people to smoke pot for chronic illnesses.
(MarijuanaNews note: Why do the patients want something that does not work? The fact is that most of the people who are trying to get their doctor's help are already using cannabis, and just want to be safe from arrest.

Have the quacks done exhaustive research on therapeutic benefits of being arrested? And have they determined that hand-cuffs have no side-effects? Does being terrified and humiliated not cause disphoria?)

Officials with the palliative care program in Edmonton have decided not to support those applications.
See
Cruelty, Incompetence, And Quackery Threaten Canadian Medical Cannabis Patients.

De Kock said they want to see the effectivness of pot proven in clinical trials before they will recommend it.

" It's fraught with practical as well as ethical difficulties, " she said. " Many or most of the patients at the end of their lives are too sick to be interested in being involved with research studies. "
(MarijuanaNews note: Ethical difficulties? Of course, terminally ill patients should not be used as guinea pigs, but there are huge numbers of patients in Canada and DEAland who are using cannabis medically, and they are being ignored by the quacks, and persecuted by the narks. Even the seven remaining patients who receive legal cannabis from the DEAland Federal government are not studied by the medical profession. There is a huge amount of data available through the Canadian and DEAland compassion clubs, but it is also being ignored. That is bad medicine and bad science.)
